column3: “Words” (the first) is rendered “speech.”
“On my palate” is rendered “in my mouth.”
NASB supplies “are from”; “purified” is rendered “sincerely.”
“Spirit” is capitalized in NASB.
“Respond to me” is rendered “Refute me.”
“Like your mouth to God” is rendered “I belong to God like you,” and “nipped off” as “formed.”
“Will not terrify … will not be heavy” is rendered with “should.”
“In my ears” is rendered “in my hearing”; NASB supplies “your.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Occasions” is rendered “pretexts”; NASB adds “invents.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“I will answer you” is rendered “let me tell you.”
“All his words he does not answer” is rendered “He does not give an account of all His doings.”
“Once … twice” is kept; NASB supplies “yet.”
“Deep sleep” is rendered “sound sleep.”
“Uncover the ear” is rendered “opens the ears,” and “seals with their discipline” as “seals their instruction.”
The Hebrew reads “to turn aside a person a deed”; NASB has “turn man aside from his conduct.” “Cover” is rendered “keep … from.”
“By the missile” is rendered “into Sheol”; the Hebrew word may mean a weapon or a channel, and the meaning is uncertain.
The written text has “multitude,” the reading aloud “strife”; NASB has “unceasing complaint.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Laid bare” is rendered “stick out”; the written and read forms differ.
Close to the Hebrew.
“Uprightness” is rendered “what is right,” and “tell” as “remind.”
“Showed favor” is rendered “let him be gracious.”
“Grows fresh” is rendered with “Let.” The meaning of the first verb is uncertain.
“He saw his face” is rendered “That he may see His face.”
“Watches over” is rendered “will sing to”; the meaning is uncertain. “It was not equal to me” is rendered “it is not proper for me.”
The written text reads “my soul,” the reading aloud “his soul”; NASB follows the written “my.”
“Two times three times” is rendered “oftentimes.”
Close to the Hebrew.
